candidate_passages.text: - A new chapter in the **same location** keeps every surviving item and the player's layout. The chapter boundary must never automatically carry/import earlier-location items, prune items, rearrange the work surface or re-grant existing stock. It does not start a fresh board or pretend to travel.

- **Artwork is now authorized:** use vivid, clearly visible persistent background art for each setting, shared across its chapters; preserve contrast with local backing behind labels and controls. Decorative scenery must not imply inventory or completed work that is not present. Movable objects, labels and tasks remain independently legible.

- **Fixed phone-like panels:** a location has a bounded 390 × 844 logical reference area, responsive down to narrow phones and compact on desktop. It never grows to fit more objects. Previously visited panels stay visible above it, with vertical scrollback and deliberate dragging between discovered locations. Storage ownership is separate from the story's active location; moving an object backward does not restart travel, grant stock or change its provenance.

- Created objects may overlap reasonably; there must be a way to select them. Normal authored play should not demand housekeeping. Arrival-stock packing must not create new overlaps by squeezing a carried arrangement; removing genuine empty gaps and moving rigid clusters on first arrival is different from rearranging residents. Source cards retain their full readable size.

- A genuine commercial kitchen station (pastry bench, hot line, confectionery counter) may be a distinct location. An explicit later shift can also have a new panel in the same physical setting: explain the time change and cleared workspace, retain the earlier panel, and bring actual prepared food forward. Never use an arbitrary chapter reset as a disguised cleanup.

- Normal partner highlighting is a core affordance: show it on press/selection and throughout a thing-drag, including hotspot operands and relevant current-goal things. Hotspot frames are fixed targets, not draggable things. Show legal existing partners and valid drops, not future output-name previews. Highlights must not disappear merely because a source is gold or a target is a hotspot; they must not promise an illegal direction or an already-existing result.

- Never create another C when that output already exists, including in an earlier location or fitted construction. Moving, fitting or incorporating an output is not permission to reconstruct a duplicate. Alternative routes should converge on existing output identities where appropriate; distinct real objects in different kitchens can still share a familiar label.

- After a successful creation, surviving dragged A returns to its original position; B stays put. New C appears close to the receiving B, or **inside the hotspot target** when the hotspot is the operand, and remains portable rather than permanently attached. The explicit transformation and installation rules below take precedence over this ordinary birth rule. A same-token drop is a no-op/rejection, never deletion.

Clear, simple object names are a mandatory baseline, not an optional polish pass. Assume the player skips chapter prose, cache narrative, item descriptions and Read. The task list, object/hotspot names, text printed on tiles, visible fitted components and normal interaction feedback must make the action intelligible. A short quotation already printed on a tile counts; a crucial premise hidden behind Read does not.

- A key quotation can be the item itself: 5–12 words need not collapse into an icon. All long labels—including observations and cases—need matching line space in tile rendering and engine packing. Reserve the reader for fuller source context; never attach fake readings just to obtain text space.
- Celebrate an actually achieved invention. An unfinished Rover shell is not a working Rover; required fitted parts and the authored capability must be present before celebrating it.

- Keep ordinary combinations uncelebrated and never replay an old-save backlog as newly earned. A dismissed celebration happens once per run. Pending rewards and acknowledgement survive saving; Undo removes unearned pending events but does not repeat a dismissed triumph. Reset starts a fresh run; debug checkpoints identify their replayed achievements as historical.

- Each recipe explicitly declares every object input as `transform`, `incorporate`, or `retain`, with a reason. An upgrade or physical incorporation consumes its original at the event when no independent use needs an outside copy; reusable tools and supplies remain when another use still needs them. This is not a finite-stock simulation or a blanket everything-stays rule. Exhausting an input's future uses is a warning to review its lifecycle, never permission to delete it automatically.

- Adding to a fitted rover should keep the same recognisable rover and its fitted parts. Prefer installation in its existing slots. Never collapse a compound into an apparently simple object. When joining assemblies or genuinely changing an assembly's identity, explicitly preserve and display its existing components through subsequent transformations. A change of name is not a disassembly.

- An enhanced thing satisfies the function it genuinely retains: an upgraded radio or growing shelter must not fail merely because its name changed. Preserve real functional distinctions; a radio's little supply is not automatically a rover's traction power. No exact-name barrier should manufacture extra work.

- Every non-opening chapter must meaningfully use at least one, preferably several, objects or ideas created in an earlier chapter. An item merely remaining in inventory, or an old raw supply, does not satisfy this.

- Distinguish actual new supplies spatially: existing objects above a dotted “new items” line, actual deliveries below. Do not use New/Carried labels or divide the screen into arbitrary halves. Compact genuine empty vertical gaps only when needed, without introducing new overlaps; fixed locations remain bounded. The first intentional committed crossing or successful cross-group combination removes the line; cancellation, rejection, reading, resizing and reload do not. Undo restores the earlier split. The lower group contains only this arrival's actual fresh grants, never old-location spillover or existing things reclassified as new. Crossing is scoped to those groups in that location. With no fresh delivery, do not add a divider or rearrange settled objects; old saves are not retroactively relaid out.

- A kitchen or cooking station should support several services, with ordinary ingredients and tools introduced when its stores become available, not a fresh box of bespoke materials for each chapter. Keep the active work surface manageable; a substantial facility may have small, clearly established workrooms. New chapters on the same work surface must not repack or relocate settled objects.

- Entering a skipped chapter still introduces its genuine caches and hotspots. Supplies remain tangible with their original provenance and new-versus-old classification through a cascade; never fabricate combinations or invention rewards. Empty source locations do not retain a delivery divider.

- Every recipe should earn its place through a meaningful, recognisable result or use, not graph padding. Every non-opening chapter must meet the earlier-created-item continuity rule above; merely carrying an item is not meaningful reuse. Historical influence, analogy and physical lifecycle are different claims and need different evidence.

- Grade **factual/authenticity accuracy** and **forward player intuition/useful purpose** separately. A historically or physically defensible account can still fail the player-facing test; an authenticity reviewer must not approve a contrived recipe merely because it can be explained afterwards.

Historical contracts remain intact. In particular, old automatic-hiding rules, permanent past-stage gold, compulsory equipment-delivery chores, chapter-equals-travel assumptions, and the proposed alternating Mars narrators are superseded where they conflict with this document. Frozen source manifests and test evidence describe their pinned revisions; update current behaviour through an explicit successor, never rewrite an old audit to claim it already proved the new direction.

- Fitting the vestibule’s tie downs and insulating blanket are independent jobs. Either order must finish the same secured, insulated vestibule, preserving its fitted pieces and position. An intermediate may represent a genuinely incomplete assembly, but must not add a mandatory operation.

headings: Elemental Game Research and Invention Handoff
Reveal recipes without revealing the whole answer
Use AI playtests as diagnostic evidence
Keep the player blind to implementation
Inspect behaviour rather than a single fun score
Judge the experience and decide what to change
Bring in people before declaring success
Plan comparisons that can change your mind

candidate_passages.text: - Avoid repeated crafting chores. A consumed or destroyed deployment may cost another action to replace; it must not require rebuilding the same ingredient chain.

- Run a closed loop: state a hypothesis about fun, implement a small test, play it, inspect evidence, change the design and play again. Reject attractive ideas when the evidence does not support them.
- World state: particular walls, fires, weather effects, creatures and terrain. These can expire, move, be destroyed or interact. Their behaviour must be readable.

- Scarce decisions: actions before a threat arrives, deployment locations, or a simple commitment allowance. Start with one main source of scarcity. Unlimited conceptual supply must not permit unlimited instantaneous deployment.

Begin with all currently legal novel recipes in a small content set. If the menu becomes unwieldy, compare a curated offer of three or four with the full menu. Curation must not randomly withhold the only survival move. Test offer fairness separately from tactical skill.

Sid Meier's 2012 talk frames gameplay through interesting decisions. [4] The design hypothesis here is that revealed recipes can support situational tradeoffs: immediate relief versus a more powerful future capability. Soren Johnson's account of working with Meier advocates repeated prototyping and substantial changes that expose the design space. [5] Neither is a formula guaranteeing that every choice is enjoyable.

For this project, hypothesise that fun comes from understandable agency, curiosity about new capabilities, consequential commitment, and the satisfaction of a plan working or being intelligently revised. The player should feel inventive. Pressure is useful only if it sharpens those experiences. Explore whether relief, beauty or playful absurdity improve them; reject the assumption that more pressure always means more fun.

Extend the research with designer postmortems and contrasting views. For each source record author, date, direct URL, actual claim, practical implication and limitation. Distinguish a talk description from a watched talk, a paraphrase from a quotation, and our hypothesis from the source's conclusion. Avoid unsupported neuroscience and universal claims.
1. State one hypothesis: for example, spending a turn on discovery creates enjoyable tension between invention and survival. Specify what evidence would contradict it.

Give each fresh player only the rules and observations a human would receive. No source code, hidden recipe graph, future seed, privileged world state or external walkthrough. Reveal available recipes exactly as the game does. A separate evaluator may inspect internals, but must label that access. Use original recipe content to reduce memorised solutions.
- Plan revision: identify where a discovery or world response changes the next action for a sensible reason. A polished explanation must agree with the replay.
If no humans can play, complete the useful AI and mechanical work and state exactly what remains unvalidated. Never invent participants, quotations, ratings, preferences or human conclusions.
- An iteration log: hypothesis, change, predicted effect, observed evidence, decision and next experiment. Preserve at least three substantive cycles or explain an early rejection.

Initial experiential target: understand a threatened place, choose among plausible inventions, see a plan matter, and revise it after consequences. Hypothesis H1: a turn spent discovering creates worthwhile anticipation only when the new capability has an immediate, readable consequence and there is room to recover.

Potential falsifiers: planning degenerates into one winning recipe chain; discovery is dominated by repeatedly deploying a cheap stopgap; successful traces are long maintenance loops; blind players mispredict effects despite reading their cards; the grader prefers verbose traces or number of recipes over actual consequential decisions.

Executable grader emits support/concern/unknown evidence cards, not a fun total. Eight adversarial feature fixtures plus real false-prediction and late-unused-discovery traces test rhetoric, cosmetic variety, forced chains, repairs, luck and missing human evidence. Detected a methodological trap: the informed solver's small known-concept/stability bonuses can encourage irrelevant late discoveries, while AI players choose to wait. Added explicit unused-discovery reporting; raw discovery count is never evidence of fun. Random policy seed mixing fixed before the final development/holdout screens because consecutive LCG first samples had highly correlated openings.
### User correction — kill the dashboard and put combining under the hand

Decision: stop treating the flood/dashboard as the default or a framework future games must inherit. Retain it at ?experiment=flood as evidence. Rebuild the default as a sparse table left and Things shelf right. Two actual ingredient pieces start on the table. Dragging one onto another is the committed combination; contact previews the result, releasing merges them there, the result itself can be handled and combined again. Reuse is a physical copy from the shelf, not a recipe/output command. Available partners light up under the hand; no blind-recipe puzzle is required. Keep the new surface as an explicitly bounded interaction experiment before selecting a surrounding challenge. Do not claim that removing the dashboard alone creates a good game.

Hypothesis H5: direct handling, contact feedback and a persistent manipulable result restore the perception that the player is doing the combining. Falsifiers: fresh browser players cannot make the first mix using the screen alone; they look for an output menu; result placement or shelf reuse surprises them; repeated pieces obscure the gesture; more animation hides unclear contact. A browser bridge now exposes only actual screen images/visible controls and real mouse/key input, so fresh agents cannot substitute the headless action API for playing the UI. Physical feel/enjoyment still needs the user's/human judgment.

The agent disliked previews listing outcomes and I queued removing partner outcome names. The HUMAN OWNER then spontaneously praised exactly that hover discovery as a masterstroke removing the Doodle God ontology frustration, while finding the cross-icon placement only slightly confusing and deferring that detail. CANCELLED label removal before implementation; the original hover outcome revelation remains. This disagreement must remain in the grader, not be smoothed into model consensus. One owner review is real human feedback about this affordance, separate from a recruited playtest and from proof that the whole game is fun.

The owner explicitly confirmed the new contract: low-level search for legal combinations is not the source of fun; an intellectual/skill challenge must sit above combinations the player can inspect. Rejection test added in docs/design-contract.md: a challenge must remain worthwhile with every legal pair/result inspectable. The combining gesture remains the primary player action. Sources of timing, sequence, spatial, process or inferential challenge are candidates; hiding recipes is not a fallback. New gesture-evidence grader keeps physical-input evidence, agent reports, actual human feedback and untested challenge/enjoyment distinct.

This is a design interpretation to explore, not a verified exclusive theory of history. Logistics can be a capability the player creates without becoming supply management. Check the obvious dominance problem before building a large simulation: if every safety capability is harmless to acquire, learn all of them first. candidate_passages.text: > **Historical policy candidate (15:00 UTC update):** This freeze predates the user’s new instruction that finished objects remain tangible where made, with removal only for upgrade/incorporation and explicit travel to physical areas. Its hiding/bench behavior does **not** satisfy that new instruction. The already-running source-blind trial must complete unchanged and be interpreted only as evidence about the prior policy. No favorable count or trial result here validates the new persistent-object design.

Correctly honoring obvious shortcuts materially reduces duration. Final frozen V2 has an **exact minimum of 44 successful creations from four elements**, or **24 more from the existing authored 22-creation checkpoint**. A deliberate set of richer alternative endings has a minimal authored route of **70 creations from four elements**. These are solver results legally replayed through the model—not observed human decisions. The proposed 80–130-successful-creation hypothesis is **not met**, and no step was inserted just to cross 80. The optional ontology is larger than any required story route. Comfortable crafting counts as meaningful progress; nothing here demands that each action be a strategic dilemma.

Six freely selectable work areas—hearth, garden, workshop, shore, study, courtyard—organize intentions. There is also a current-invitation view. Changing place changes only a projection, never recipes, discoveries, capabilities or legality. No ingredient is consumed or manually packed/unpacked.

The current-invitation view alone is insufficient: up to **66 legal recipes have both ingredients hidden there** in the tested states. Every one is available on its owning place's bench, and every one-hidden pair is surfaced by selecting its visible operand. This is a verifiable retrieval rule, not proof that a player will know where to look. Free place navigation must be discoverable, and must not become another inventory-management chore. The source-blind trial is needed specifically to challenge that tradeoff.

Still questionable: Earth + Stone → Ore, Planks + Stone → Wheel, Pulley + Wood → Crane, Glass + Water → Lens, and oil/lye chemistry compress substantial real processes. That is consistent with the established storybook genre, but player plausibility is not established by source-aware agreement. The graph is not marketed as a chemistry or engineering lesson.

A fresh player must receive only `docs/PLAYER-INSTRUCTIONS.txt`, a fresh session name and the wrapper—not minima, output totals, desired conclusions or these reports. Full wrapper records go to `trials/SESSION/chronological-capture.jsonl` with raw stdout/stderr bytes and exit codes; `finish` or `stop` saves terminal state. The player may stop voluntarily. Their qualitative report and raw input history must be preserved even if unfavorable.

This research currently establishes a larger coherent executable hypothesis and a plausible bounded workspace rule, **not ~200 enjoyable decisions**. The next empirical question is whether goals, optional exploration and clear progress make players want to continue without managing a catalog. Distinguish meaningful attempted combinations, successful discoveries, navigation, hints and repeated failures. Do not count interface actions or failed guesses toward the target merely to improve a number.

candidate_passages.text: Use JSON matching ../schema/scenario.ts. All IDs are unique stable lowercase strings. Item IDs and location IDs must be distinct. Locations are referenced as `@location-id` only when they are an operand in recipe a/b. Ordinary two-item recipes are commutative. `at` requires the acted-on target to be placed at that location (A+B at P); a recipe without `at` does not silently change by location. Ambiguous pair/setting rules are rejected.

Create recipes have `out`; installation recipes instead have `install:{target:ITEM_KIND,slot:SLOT_ID,component:ITEM_KIND}`. The two operand kinds must match that target/component. A slot is declared on the target Item. Required slots gate its declared capabilities until all are filled. Installed parts grant only slot-declared capabilities, not every capability of arbitrary nested parts. Required slots are unnamed in player view until filled; optional empty slots are hidden. An installation is counted as one successful combination, separately from creating a new item. Components remain outside if still useful; otherwise they are incorporated. To upgrade a slot, explicitly list compatible successive components in its accepts list; each different installation is a distinct recipe.

`retire` is only for a conceptual upgrade/incorporation, with a reason. The engine never auto-hides terminal things. It removes an explicit retired input only when no unfinished recipe or remaining objective still needs that exact kind/capability. Items and discoveries are globally unique, including incorporated components; recipes never recreate an already discovered output. Historical retained item states are not reset between stages.

Initial supplies are initialItems. Later primitive supplies need a named cache with contextual narrative and broad plausible contents. A cache ID opens once. Locations appear only where declared in a stage, remain fixed in that area, and are never duplicated or teleported. Previously visited areas can be revisited with selected actual carried things. Stage advance carries useful existing things as one translated group; default is conservative future usefulness. Optional stage `carry` lists kinds of existing things to take instead, never creates them; authored carry must preserve a legal future route. This lets trials diagnose over-carrying rather than hide things. Empty old areas persist in world state.

Source/caveat metadata is developer evidence, not chronology asserted by the engine. Recipe descriptions appear only after discovery. Player interface exposes current things, motivation, explicit objectives, available areas and compatible partners, never unknown output names or hidden recipe IDs. Debug checkpoints are legal action replays, not injected state.

Automatic chapter carry takes only objects actually present in the departure area. It never retrieves an object left in an earlier area; use explicit travel carrying the selected real tools. Earlier locations never move. Conservative default carry may carry more objects than the intended route requires; that is a clutter diagnostic, not a reason to hide objects. Explicit carry lists cannot override physical continuity.

Only take things useful for the current scene, not everything useful in the future. `Stage.carry` is an authoritative list of known item identities to collect for this scene. It never creates an undiscovered item. When omitted, `sceneCarry` follows current objective prerequisites backward, stopping at an existing intermediate rather than taking its obsolete raw ancestors; alternative recipe routes and required construction parts are included. It does not consider future stages. Authors can include local optional combinations by listing their known useful operands explicitly.

Narrative travel abstracts collecting known tools from still-accessible earlier areas. Tokens are moved, never copied; `Event.transfers` records `{item,from,to}` and the action message explains collecting needed things along the way. Each source group's relative arrangement is retained. Things already in the destination remain untouched. Unneeded tangible items remain where left. Locations remain fixed. No closed-area, immovable-item or object-to-location mechanic has been added. Authors should not ask to pack a bridge as a tool: use portable observations/records or keep that scene there.

The conservative carry rule includes any remaining legal recipe use and future objective use; authored route analysis must measure clutter before refining carry. Save validation is structural, not a cryptographic proof of legitimate play. No artificial timer/resource pressure is included. State mutations must go through ordinary combine/place/move/advance/visit actions.

Ask for sparse open reports: what the player was trying to accomplish, any confusing or arbitrary relation, something satisfying, and whether they would freely continue. Comfortable obvious progress can be worthwhile; not every action must be a strategic dilemma.

No item contains an actual time, angle, clock drift, east/west direction, numeric table entry, disagreement or final range. `make-time-difference` promises a “stated conversion,” but no player-visible conversion is stated. `make-position-comparison` promises to compare two answers whose answers never exist. `make-navigation-chart` promises an uncertainty range without specifying one. The sea-trial context is real (`make-voyage-clock-record.at = sea-trial`); preserve it, but put an actual changed clock result there.

There is also a bounded reasoning gap: cumulative flow exceeding instantaneous stock does not alone exclude a one-way system with replenishment. The candidate never specifies the rival replenishment capacity. Harvey's own chapter IX explicitly combines the quantity argument with inadequate food supply and venous return. The toy numbers are correctly attributed as invented, but that attribution does not supply the missing premise. [Harvey, chapter IX and conclusion](https://bertie.ccsu.edu/naturesci/evolution/unit10background/HarveyNine.html).
### 4. High — the observatory never identifies the test or the next question it supposedly learns to ask
- `trial-menu` says four light × nutrient comparisons, but `experiment-lattice` never displays their cases.
- `distinguishing-trial` never says which case is chosen or what each rival predicts.

- `surprising-bloom` has an actual event, **“Bloom in the dark,”** but a nutrient-centered rival might predict that. There is no visible adopted model or nutrient condition making this event a falsification rather than confirmation of one of the existing rivals.
- `next-question` never states a question. `make-learning-observatory` announces that the apparatus now chooses a falsifiable next test, but the player cannot identify that test.

Yet `day-night-record` contains no sequence to inspect; `adaptive-cycle` names no chosen observation; `seasonal-city-rule` names no production/shade change; `symbiont-change` says only that a partner changes behavior. `make-evolving-city` takes that change and immediately awards the final city without a defined changed output or response. candidate_passages.text: Both `author.py` and the frozen `fresh-pastry-v1/scenario.json` specify `at: saucepan` only for flour + butter → white roux. candidate_passages.text: - **Repeated ovens.** There are 31 stationary locations over 20 chapters, generally one or two per chapter and never more than three. Most are ordinary heat sources. They do not require construction, but repeated oven drops may still become routine. Preserve the meaningful cool-bench/hot-pan contrast; test whether other cooking destinations earn their footprint.

- **Narrative is not chronology.** The moving caravan is a framing fiction for historical techniques. It must not be advertised as an accurate chronological history or a documented chain from a particular hearth culture to Hostess.

- **Minor formula compression.** The game names real products but is not a recipe. Full sponge, marzipan, quick-bread and commercial-cake formulations are more constrained than the graph. Never market the logical test as food-science or safety validation.

Keep the candidate isolated and source-testable. Retain the archived four-scene starter and saucepan pilot. Do not deploy or replace them on the strength of solvability. Focus the next independent playtest on pastry→sauce and precision→packaged cake; use the shorter orchard→soup segment if the question is whether old food actually feels valuable. The player must not receive this graph, the 185-count target, or the authored route.

Three source-stage export preparations—fruit syrup, vanilla custard and sifted flour—must be earned before later chapters can use them. They currently appear as intermediate goals that reveal local dish goals. This represents a preparation/service order, **not** a literal ingredient dependency of those local dishes. Independent final preparation goals would be a cleaner alternative if the reveal feels artificial; removing the requirement and conjuring the missing ingredient later would not. This issue was sent to the parent for review rather than concealed by the passing objective validator.

The final adversarial route has a slightly larger scene than the ordinary witnesses: up to 12 arrival items and 20 live items after deliberately retrieving extra milk/sugar. Normal canonical/exhaustive routes remain at 11/19. A browser test, not these counts, must judge the practical footprint.

candidate_passages.text: - Art is a later phase. Do not add it before the user asks.

- Each recipe explicitly declares every object input as `transform`, `incorporate`, or `retain`, with a reason. Exhausting an input's future uses is a warning to review its lifecycle, never permission to delete it automatically.

- Adding to a fitted rover should keep the same recognisable rover and its fitted parts. Prefer installation in its existing slots. Never collapse a compound into an apparently simple object. When joining assemblies or genuinely changing an assembly's identity, explicitly preserve and display its existing components through subsequent transformations. A change of name is not a disassembly.

- Every non-opening chapter must meaningfully use at least one, preferably several, objects or ideas created in an earlier chapter. An item merely remaining in inventory, or an old raw supply, does not satisfy this.

candidate_passages.text: Use JSON matching ../schema/scenario.ts. All IDs are unique stable lowercase strings. Item IDs and location IDs must be distinct. Locations are referenced as `@location-id` only when they are an operand in recipe a/b. Ordinary two-item recipes are commutative. `at` requires the acted-on target to be placed at that location (A+B at P); a recipe without `at` does not silently change by location. Ambiguous pair/setting rules are rejected.

Create recipes have `out`; installation recipes instead have `install:{target:ITEM_KIND,slot:SLOT_ID,component:ITEM_KIND}`. The two operand kinds must match that target/component. A slot is declared on the target Item. Required slots gate its declared capabilities until all are filled. Installed parts grant only slot-declared capabilities, not every capability of arbitrary nested parts. Required slots are unnamed in player view until filled; optional empty slots are hidden. An installation is counted as one successful combination, separately from creating a new item. Components remain outside if still useful; otherwise they are incorporated. To upgrade a slot, explicitly list compatible successive components in its accepts list; each different installation is a distinct recipe.

`retire` is only for a conceptual upgrade/incorporation, with a reason. The engine never auto-hides terminal things. It removes an explicit retired input only when no unfinished recipe or remaining objective still needs that exact kind/capability. Items and discoveries are globally unique, including incorporated components; recipes never recreate an already discovered output. Historical retained item states are not reset between stages.

Initial supplies are initialItems. Later primitive supplies need a named cache with contextual narrative and broad plausible contents. A cache ID opens once. Locations appear only where declared in a stage, remain fixed in that area, and are never duplicated or teleported. Previously visited areas can be revisited with selected actual carried things. Stage advance carries useful existing things as one translated group; default is conservative future usefulness. Optional stage `carry` lists kinds of existing things to take instead, never creates them; authored carry must preserve a legal future route. This lets trials diagnose over-carrying rather than hide things. Empty old areas persist in world state.

Source/caveat metadata is developer evidence, not chronology asserted by the engine. Recipe descriptions appear only after discovery. Player interface exposes current things, motivation, explicit objectives, available areas and compatible partners, never unknown output names or hidden recipe IDs. Debug checkpoints are legal action replays, not injected state.

Automatic chapter carry takes only objects actually present in the departure area. It never retrieves an object left in an earlier area; use explicit travel carrying the selected real tools. Earlier locations never move. Conservative default carry may carry more objects than the intended route requires; that is a clutter diagnostic, not a reason to hide objects. Explicit carry lists cannot override physical continuity.

Only take things useful for the current scene, not everything useful in the future. `Stage.carry` is an authoritative list of known item identities to collect for this scene. It never creates an undiscovered item. When omitted, `sceneCarry` follows current objective prerequisites backward, stopping at an existing intermediate rather than taking its obsolete raw ancestors; alternative recipe routes and required construction parts are included. It does not consider future stages. Authors can include local optional combinations by listing their known useful operands explicitly.

Narrative travel abstracts collecting known tools from still-accessible earlier areas. Tokens are moved, never copied; `Event.transfers` records `{item,from,to}` and the action message explains collecting needed things along the way. Each source group's relative arrangement is retained. Things already in the destination remain untouched. Unneeded tangible items remain where left. Locations remain fixed. No closed-area, immovable-item or object-to-location mechanic has been added. Authors should not ask to pack a bridge as a tool: use portable observations/records or keep that scene there.

`Stage.completionText?:string` states what happens after the scene's actual objectives are satisfied. It never changes eligibility. It is absent from the player's view until all current objectives are true; ordinary action output appends it only on the transition from incomplete to complete. Reversing a placement clears the completion view. Final advance uses the authored ending instead of the generic completion sentence. Intermediate actions while the goals remain satisfied do not repeat the ending.

candidate_passages.text: The substantial chain below develops **water lifting and useful power**, then branches to lighting, communication, material processing and mobility. It is not a claim that one pump must be built in every solution. Gravity-fed service, direct mechanical pumping, moving the use site, or an alternative source must remain legal when their actual properties suffice.

This is a content allocation, **not a list of mandatory discoveries or a count target**. Some candidate nodes may merge when their functional differences are too weak. A clear glass sheet and a polished lens should not be distinguished by a hidden quality flag; if focusing/faithful imaging is proposed, its visible geometry and effect must be explicit. Conversely, not every intermediate needs a unique late-game goal to justify comfortable construction or curiosity.
| B | That material + a disclosed physical form | Actual cavity/channel/contact geometry | Other forms or an already suitable natural shape work. No “must take-form” stamp. |

| N | Pump + real source + watertight receiving conduit | Water reaches an actual higher receiving surface | Height/source connectivity must be a consistent new law. No pump badge if the old abstract link already teleports water uphill. |

- A **source-supported electrical installation** can power a heater, lamp, motor or communication emitter. Those devices must have different actual effects; “connect four named consumers” alone would repeat the old network problem.

In particular, a coherent implementation would need to decide whether to add **mechanical work/coupling**, **height-sensitive fluid service**, and **live communication**. These are substantial new laws, not content rows falsely presented as existing engine behavior. Do not add pressure equations, resource rates, fuel tanks or realistic manufacturing chemistry. A minimal property-and-port model can be public and deterministic, but must be defined consistently before claiming feasibility.

- Some sophisticated components may be available as recovered objects or complete-catalogue capabilities. The normal condition must state its starting level clearly; do not remove supplied devices after observing a short route.

- A single canonical output may bundle a useful familiar internal arrangement after discovery. Learned capability must genuinely reduce future setup rather than merely unlock a longer repeated fabrication animation.
- A recipe graph must be shared across purposes. Independent disjoint trees labeled “communication,” “water” and “mobility” are not evidence of transfer.

candidate_passages.text: A wound is harm suffered; stealing the meal is a wrong deliberately chosen. Comparing them as losses must not turn suffering into evidence of guilt.
The case deliberately removes personal acts. If the infant still needs forgiveness, the explanation must concern something besides an act the infant chose.
Knowing what is right has not been enough to make the person do it. Augustine argues that God's help must address willing and acting as well as ignorance.
- Two Principles: good and evil must have opposed sources

Augustine says evil is damage within a good creation. The writer of the Book of Two Principles argues that a wholly good source cannot cause evil, so evil must have an opposed source. The two accounts give different answers to the same problem of suffering and wrongdoing.
- The writer turns the tree saying into a rule about causes [preserve] + Case: the same world feeds people and destroys them -> Two Principles: good and evil must have opposed sources
- Two Principles: good and evil must have opposed sources + `augustine-loss` [preserve] -> `origins-dispute`
- Two Principles: no evil can come from a wholly good cause + Case: the same world feeds people and destroys them -> Two Principles: good and evil must have opposed sources
- Fire can work well as fire while harming something else [preserve] + Two Principles: good and evil must have opposed sources -> Aquinas: harmful effects do not require a separate evil source

> NOTE: Source completion text, retained for author reference rather than an additional completion popup: Aquinas says fire can function well as fire while harming something else. That challenges the claim that harm must come from a wholly evil source, but leaves the creator's responsibility in question.
The Son addresses the Father. Augustine must explain how this real relationship belongs within his belief in one God.
After the blessing, the bread looks and tastes the same. Aquinas's account must explain why he still says that what it is has changed.
The text does not discard bodily life. Work and discipline remain, but their role must be distinguished from earning acceptance.

Calvin's writings from 1543–1559 raise objections about prayer, images and relics. Compare asking a living friend to pray, asking a departed saint and honouring a religious picture or relic. Calvin objects to particular practices and claims; the cases must be considered separately.

0959c0d1fa024934c46c449eda1057effe778c82.disposition: reference-only: original claims and provenance preserved

candidate_passages.text: > NOTE: Recipes are global. Items lists provide the sources and optional constructions relevant to that session; a listed construction must still be made. All single-condition goals use the inline form and latch when satisfied. Separate evening and next-morning sessions remain separate chapters even when their picture is reused. The new format brings needed work forward and does not reopen an earlier board.
A valid argument has a conclusion that must follow if its starting claims are true. It still matters whether those claims are actually true.
- Must we reach a verdict? -- "A judgment left suspended"
Euclid builds geometry from stated definitions and starting assumptions. Later claims must be supported by proofs.
Translators carry arguments about logic and nature into Arabic. Their choices must preserve meanings, not simply replace one set of words with another.
Bright light affects the eye, giving a reason to study incoming light. Never look directly at the Sun to test this.
A formal debate states an objection before attempting to answer it. The reply must address the difficulty rather than ignore it.
- "An explanation adds an entity it never uses"
Do not add things to an explanation when they do no work. A shorter explanation is not automatically true; it must still account for the evidence.
- "Different questions about why" + "An explanation adds an entity it never uses" [preserve] -> "Do not multiply idle explanations"
- "Revelation makes claims reason must interpret"
- "Avicenna: a necessary source of existence" [preserve] + "Revelation makes claims reason must interpret" [preserve] -> "Reason and faith: distinct questions"
- Must everything circle Earth? -- "A system of moons around Jupiter"
Venus appears as a crescent at some times and nearly full at others. A model of its motion must explain this range of phases.
Repeated observations reveal Venus's full range of phases. Any successful model must account for both its crescent and nearly full appearances.
The next morning, we return to a cleared worktable. Explain apparent backward motion and compare Mars's recorded path with a circular orbit. Kepler's search for order must fit the observations.
- Must an orderly orbit be a circle? -- "A lawful sky without perfect circles"
The idea that the heavens have an orderly design motivates investigation. It is not evidence that any particular orbit must be correct.
People often notice evidence that agrees with what they already believe. Bacon warns that inquiry must also look for cases that do not fit.
- Does heat always need light? -- "Heat must be sought beyond luminous bodies"
Rubbing can warm an object without producing a flame. An account of heat must explain this case too.
- "Heat must be sought beyond luminous bodies"
Rubbing can produce warmth without a glowing source. An account that ties heat only to shining objects therefore misses an ordinary case and must be reconsidered.
- "Brightness need not bring comparable felt warmth" [preserve] + "Rubbing warms without flame" [preserve] -> "Heat must be sought beyond luminous bodies"
- "Heat must be sought beyond luminous bodies" [preserve] + `matched-wood` [preserve] -> "Rubbing changes the warming in this comparison"
Living animals feed, grow and repair themselves. A moving mechanical figure must be compared with more than an animal's outward motion.
The heart pumps blood out through arteries. This outward flow must be considered alongside blood returning through veins.

Newton describes motion on Earth and in the sky in one system. He assumes space exists independently of the objects in it, and time passes alike everywhere. Later theories must explain both the system's successes and its limits.
Kant asks what the mind must contribute for experience to be possible. His response addresses a philosophical problem rather than disproving Hume with one experiment.
- Do universal rights include women? -- "Universal reason must include women"
The declaration claims rights for everyone. Its claim must be compared with who actually receives those rights.
- "A claim to rights beyond inherited rank" + "Women denied the education invoked for equality" [preserve] -> "Universal reason must include women"
- "1801: plantation cultivation must not stop"
- "Locke: legitimate government rests on consent" + "1801: plantation cultivation must not stop" [preserve] -> "Compulsory cultivation challenges consent"
Some kinds of animals no longer exist. A catalogue of life must therefore include a past that differs from the present.
- Must Earth's changes happen at one pace? -- "Long processes and abrupt events"
Offspring have inherited differences and face limited resources. These facts alone do not show which differences will leave more descendants; reproductive outcomes must also be compared.
In Marx's critique, workers can lose control over their activity and its products. The problem is a relationship of ownership and power, not simply disliking a task.
- "Distant stations must coordinate their clocks"
- "Clock coordination travels over a network" + "Distant stations must coordinate their clocks" [preserve] -> "A shared railway time"

It is evening. The worktable is cleared for a new session. Compare a freely falling room with Einstein's geometric account of gravity. The deflection of starlight provides a test with measurements that must be assessed.
Continents can be placed in a proposed earlier arrangement and compared. The reconstruction must fit evidence, not just look like a puzzle.
Continents move as parts of plates, changing the locations and connections of habitats. Patterns of living things must therefore be explained on a changing surface rather than a fixed map.
A transmitted signal can lose distinctions needed to recover the message. Communication design must protect those distinctions, not just send something detectable.
The words stay the same, but the imagined writer's life and purpose differ. The reader must consider whether that changes the work's meaning.
- Must a story choose one path? -- "A narrative can keep incompatible paths open"
- "Universal reason must include women" [preserve] + "A classification can naturalize domination" [preserve] -> "A universal promise can coexist with exclusion"
Modern lead contamination can distort measurements intended to date ancient material. The sample's own lead must be separated from what the laboratory adds.
The model proposes changing one condition in a test. The proposal must be checked against outcomes, not accepted because it sounds convincing.
The model proposes a test with a method people can inspect. A useful suggestion must expose what changes, what is measured and how it can be checked.
- Must everyone want the same good life? -- "A prosperous city need not prescribe one good life"

candidate_passages.text: 2. Each story is made up of a series of chapters, starting with `##`. The chapter has a name, but this name never appears in the game. (except maybe in debugging tools). There is an optional final chapter, by convention named "The End", with no goals or hotspots or items. It's only role is to convey its chapter-describing popup as the final text of the story.
- At a declaration site, you can also write an identifier first in backticks, e.g. `foo` bar. You must refer to this by its identifier `foo`.
- The goal "- A[B,C] @ H" means item A must have items B and C inside its slots, and be placed at hotspot H.

- Under an item, there can be nested sub-bullet composition rules. Each one must involve the item above it as a reagent (if the item was top level) or the result of the composition above it (otherwise). Alternatively, under an itom or nested sub-bullet there can be as a shorthand one or more "+B -> C" or "+B@H -> C" or "@H -> C". These mean: combine with the thing produced on the previous line (or if the previous line was a top-level item then combine with it). Note that this is sequential. An explicit reagent can carry an annotation, as in `+ B [consume] -> C`. To annotate the implied reagent, write the full rule with its reference and annotation.

- When you move to a new chapter, here's how we decide which items to populate it. Start with all items that are mentioned in top-level items or goals. This is our initial se of "needs". For every needed item, if currently exists as a standalone item then carry it forward into this chapter. A compound need "A[B,C]" if we have "A[B]" already only needs "C"; if we don't have anything then we need all of A,B,C. What might make a need not exist is (1) if it was never created, (2) if it was created but is marked as transformed/consumed.

- If it doesn't currently exist, and isn't marked as transformed/consumed, then we need every reagent from every possible way to produce it (which aren't themselves marked as transformed/consumed), and if there are no rules that produce it then the item must be a primitive item itself which we need. The set of "possible ways" should respect mutual exclusivity of items and transformed/consumed items. It should be done by sets, since reagent dependents may have cycles: when unfolding reagents, skip expanding an item that has already been unfolded.

- There are many ways to declare items and combinations. We will define a canonical form (e.g. every chapter declares its items, and separately has a section **Combinations** for combinations necessary to achieve the goals that haven't previously been written, and the final chapter has all additional combinations). But we won't require canonical form. Note that canonical form must preserve "which items are newly introduced in a chapter". We might write a story transformer which takes a story and rewrites it in canonical form.

- Once a goal is satisfied, we never take it away again. For instance if the goal was to place item A on hotspot H, once that's satisfied, then it remains satisfied even if the user moves it off again.
